goals.title: The coast you dig
goals.critique: This is round 1's 'Dig the sea in' reworded, but it adds the thing that pitch lacked: nothing resets. A coastline that keeps every dig and every breach is a reason to come back, and people would describe the game by it. The road is more honest too: a shallow-water solver on a height field is buildable, where Maelstrom at beach scale was never proven. What is still weak is the claim that 'any player' digs. The island has one player and one bird, so the map of everyone's digging is mostly Lumi's and the human's, and the pitch never says what makes tomorrow's dig different from today's beyond fixing what broke. The time-lapse is the one strong clip; the breach-and-bark moment is the same one round 1 already had.

goals.title: Lumi has a real body
goals.critique: Physics-driven clumsy bodies are a well-worn genre. Wobbly-walking and ragdoll-brawler games got there first, so a floppy bird with a balance controller is at most 5 for memorability, however good the tumble looks. Tumbles do get clipped, and the pitch sits right on the human's wish for a body that really does what it does, beak gripping and weight pulling. But mastering your own legs is a skill people tire of once the slapstick stops surprising them, and the pitch offers no reason to carry the pumpkin beyond carrying it. The road starts with an active ragdoll controller on the GPU, the hardest and riskiest piece, and nothing on it is fun until that controller works.

goals.title: Keep the fire through the night
goals.critique: Every night has a clear verb, real stakes and a clock: gather, stack, feed, don't let it die or spread. Fire as the only light is a strong showcase for a path tracer. Still, survival-campfire loops and grass fires carried by the wind have been done many times, and nothing here would make people name the game after its fire. The play is mostly fetching wood and topping up a meter until the wildfire moment, and that moment is a disaster the player avoids, so its best clip only happens when they fail. It touches 'material that burns by what it is', but it burns the world rather than building it, so the Minecraft line is weak.

goals.title: Glass the friends ask for
goals.critique: This is round 1's hot glass with a commission loop and a physical judge added. The test that shows exactly where you failed (water over the low rim onto Pickles) is the best idea in it, and it fixes round 1's low stakes a little. It is still one craft at one furnace. Wishes on a list with a clock are a familiar order-fulfilment structure, and whether blowing feels like a skill rather than a slider is still asserted, not shown. The road still rests on live thin-shell glass that inflates, sags and bursts, a research problem that was already slow last round.
